parts.latex: Find the TWO critical paths.

The function centre wants to decrease the length of each critical path by 3 hours. They can do this by hiring more staff to do ONE of the tasks so it takes less time to complete.

For which task should the centre hire more staff, and how long should that task take to ensure all tasks can be completed in 14 hours?

solutions.latex: The critical paths are $H, I, G, C$ and $H, I, K$.
criteria: Identifies a critical path, or equivalent merit

solutions.latex:
Both critical paths must shorten by 3 hours, so the task must be common to both.

The common tasks are $H$ and $I$.

$H$ takes only 2 hours, so it cannot be shortened by 3 hours.

Therefore the centre should hire more staff for task $I$, and task $I$ should take 4 hours.
criteria: Shortens a task on the critical path by 3 hours, or equivalent merit

The critical path is the longest path from start to finish. Find the earliest start time at each node.

After $A$: $3$. After $B$ or $A+C$: the larger of $5$ and $3+4=7$, so $7$.

parts.latex:
A project requires activities A to I to be completed, as shown in the table

\extable{16_q20_t1}

The minimum completion time of the project is 26 days.

The critical path includes activities B, D, G, I

Activity G took twice the time of activity I

Activity A has a float time of 3

Find the missing durations for activities A, G and I and write them into the table.

Include a network diagram below to support your answer

solutions.latex:
Let $I = x$ days, so $G = 2x$ days.

The critical path B, D, G, I has length $26$, with B and D together $11$ days.

$$\begin{aligned} 26 &= 11 + 2x + x \\ 26 &= 11 + 3x \\ x &= 5 \end{aligned}$$
Hence $I = 5$ and $G = 10$.

Path A, C, F has $C + F = 11 + 8 = 19$. Activity A has float $3$, so the path A, C, F has length $26 - 3 = 23$.

$$\begin{aligned} A + 19 &= 23 \\ A &= 4 \end{aligned}$$
$$\therefore\ A = 4,\quad G = 10,\quad I = 5$$
\exfigure{16_q20_s1}

Two correct durations, or equivalent merit

With that choice A's float is 3, as the solution requires. Please check the dummy's position against the question's precedence table, which was not supplied.

solutions.latex:
Float time of D $=$ latest start time $-$ earliest start time. First find the earliest finish of the whole project by working forwards.

$$\begin{aligned} \text{A finishes at } &2 \\ \text{B finishes at } 2+4 &= 6 \\ \text{C finishes at } 2+2 &= 4 \\ \text{F finishes at } 4+7 &= 11 \end{aligned}$$
The event at the end of F also needs E, which finishes at $6+1=7$, so its earliest time is $\max(11,7)=11$.

Then G finishes at $11+2=13$, and D finishes at $6+3=9$, so the project takes $\max(13,9) = 13$ hours.

Working backwards, D must finish by 13, so its latest start is $13-3=10$.

D's earliest start is $6$ (after B).

$$\begin{aligned} \text{Float} &= 10 - 6 \\ &= 4 \text{ hours} \end{aligned}$$
$$\therefore\ \text{option B}$$

parts.latex: What is the critical path?

The minimum time required for this project to be completed is 19 hours.

What is the duration of activity $I$?

The duration of activity $C$ is 3 hours.

What is the maximum amount of time that could occur between the start of activity $F$ and the end of activity $H$?

solutions.latex:
The critical activities have no float. Activities $A$ and $C$ have float times (their $\text{EST}\ne\text{LST}$), so they are not critical.

$$\therefore\ \text{critical path}=BEGI$$

Activity $I$ starts at its EST of 12 hours and the project takes 19 hours.

$$\begin{aligned} \text{Duration of } I &= 19-12 \\ &= 7 \text{ hours} \end{aligned}$$

$$12-3=9 \text{ hours}$$

$$9-1=8 \text{ hours}$$

The maximum time between the start of $F$ and the end of $H$ is 8 hours.

parts.latex:
The directed network shows the sequence of activities required to complete a project.

The time to complete each activity, in hours, is also shown.

\exfigure{5836_q7_1}

What is the earliest starting time (EST) in hours for activity $K$?

solutions.latex:
Activity $K$ starts at the vertex at the bottom right, where activities $F$ and $J$ finish. Its EST is the larger of the finishing times of $F$ and $J$.

Activities $C$ then $E$ come first, so $F$ and $I$ both start at
$$4+3=7$$

The vertex where $G$ and $I$ finish has EST equal to the larger of
$$4+6=10 \quad (\text{via } G)$$
$$7+2=9 \quad (\text{via } I)$$
so it is 10. Activity $J$ starts there, so $J$ finishes at $10+1=11$.

Activity $F$ starts at 7, so it finishes at $7+5=12$.

The EST of $K$ is the larger of $12$ and $11$.

$$\therefore\ \text{EST of } K = 12 \text{ hours, Option C}$$
